name: Common fly (the house fly)
change: The fly of the fly farm, as now; its real name is the house fly. It eats rot and breeds fast, and its maggots are really raised today as feed for farmed fish. Village, and anywhere with rot. Real species: Musca domestica.
reason: Already the game's fly; only the real name is new.

name: Horse fly
change: The swamps' biting fly, on the Shallow Swamp's edges and in sunny wet meadows. It flies only by day and dives at dark, moving, shiny things; only the females bite, and they bite people, the last big mammals. Its young live in the swamp mud. Real species: the black horse fly, Tabanus atratus.
reason: You kept it (D79). Its real habits give it its own play: a daytime biter with a dive you can learn, unlike the mosquito's swarm.

name: Cave fly (the scuttle fly)
change: The underground fly you asked for: a real fly of caves and ant nests that runs more than it flies, in fast, jerky bursts, so a net swung at the air misses it. It lives by the Ant Colony's granaries and in the caves; cave spiders hunt the runners, and the ones that take wing end up in glowworms' threads. Real species: the coffin fly, Conicera tibialis, a scuttle fly.
reason: Its speed is real, just on its feet. "Scuttle fly" is its plain real name.

name: Ant-decapitating fly
change: A tiny fly that lays an egg inside a fire ant; the young fly grows in the ant's head until the head falls off. The fire ants' real enemy, in the Deadly Ants zones. A player could raise and release them against fire ants, as the United States has done. Real species: Pseudacteon tricuspis.
reason: A one-of-a-kind bug with a story players will retell, and a living way to fight fire ants that comes from the ecosystem.

name: Village wasp (the paper wasp)
change: The village wasp becomes the paper wasp: its open, umbrella-shaped comb hangs under the eaves, the whole nest in plain view. It hunts caterpillars and flies, and stays calm unless you touch its nest. Real species: the European paper wasp, Polistes dominula.
reason: A gentle start that still hunts, right for a cosy village, and one of the two wasps you want (D79). Real paper wasps hunt caterpillars in numbers, which ties them to the butterflies.

name: Second wasp (the yellowjacket)
change: The game's "wasp soldier" becomes the yellowjacket of the Wasp Thicket: a hidden nest in the ground or a hollow tree, thousands of workers, stings again and again, and it chases whoever attacks it. Real species: the common wasp, Vespula vulgaris.
reason: Your second wasp (D79), and the answer to your question: wasps and hornets have no soldiers. A colony is a queen, workers and males, and every worker stings. Guarding the nest becomes something both wasps do, not a separate bug.

name: Hornet (the European hornet)
change: The game's night-hunting hornet becomes the European hornet, which really flies at night and comes to lamps, so the ranger station's lights in the Wasp Thicket (D72) will draw it. It hunts other wasps, dragonflies and mantises, and nests in hollow trees. It is the Hilltop Meadow's top threat, as that zone's plan had it. Real species: Vespa crabro.
reason: Real giant hornets fly by day, so the night hunting belongs to this one. It is one of your two hornet species (D79).

name: Giant hornet (the northern giant hornet)
change: Your giant hornet as the real one, which flies by day: it nests underground among old roots in the Millipede Forest (far ring) and raids honeybee hives in groups; a few dozen can wipe out a hive of tens of thousands. Real species: Vespa mandarinia.
reason: Your other hornet (D79), one of the most dangerous bugs here, so it lives far out. Beekeepers who set hives out near its forest have to defend them: an enemy that comes from the ecosystem, never a random event.

name: Tarantula hawk
change: A huge, rust-winged solitary wasp of Spider Vale East that stings tarantulas still and drags them to its burrow. It drinks from milkweed. Real species: Pepsis grossa.
reason: A one-of-a-kind hunter that gives the tarantulas a real enemy. Its sting is famous for pain, not harm, so a short stun would be true to life.

name: Bumblebee
change: The gentle, fuzzy bee of the Bee and Hilltop Meadows, kept in a nest box: real colonies are reared and sold to pollinate greenhouse tomatoes. It flies in cool weather when honeybees stay home and shakes pollen out of tomato flowers by buzzing, so a box in a greenhouse helps the tomatoes. It stores only a few days' food, so it gives little honey, and it rarely stings unless its nest is disturbed. Real species: the buff-tailed bumblebee, Bombus terrestris.
reason: Accepted (D81): a gentle bee for the hives beside the honey ladder, with a farm job of its own.

name: Carpenter bee
change: A big black bee that bores round holes in dead wood; the males buzz at you but can't sting. Real species: Xylocopa virginica.
reason: One of your candidates (D79). I'd leave it out in favour of the bumblebee, which has a farm job; it could come back as a village pest boring into wooden fences.

name: Honeybee
change: Where the beekeeping ladder starts, as now: hives in the village and the Bee Meadow, honey, wax and swarms, calmed with the first bee smoker. Real species: the western honey bee, Apis mellifera.
reason: Your starting bee (D80).

name: Killer bee
change: A honeybee with a fierce temper, in the hot, dry far ring (the Locust Farmland, Scorpion Rocks). It chases a threat up to 400 m and stings about ten times as often. It needs a small visual tell, such as darker bands, since real ones look the same as honeybees. It is a real upgrade, not only a danger: places with these bees make more honey, and their hives resist mites and disease better. A beekeeper tames a hive by giving it a new queen, as real beekeepers do, and needs the stronger smoker. Real species: the Africanized honey bee, a hybrid of Apis mellifera.
reason: Your more dangerous step up (D79, D80): the same species as the honeybee with a fiercer temper and a better yield, which is true to life.

name: Giant honey bee
change: Out (D82): the beekeeping bees are bees a player keeps in hives, and this one can't be kept in a hive; the rafters I proposed aren't hives. Real species: Apis dorsata.
reason: You ruled it out (D82). Keeping it on rafters went against your ask for bees kept in hives (D81).

name: Asian honey bee
change: Kept in ordinary hives, and the bee for the giant hornets' country, the Millipede Forest, where northern giant hornets wipe out honeybee hives: when a hornet raids, about 500 of its bees ball round it and heat it to 47 °C, just below the heat that kills the bees themselves. It leaves a hive more readily than the honeybee, so a neglected hive can empty, and it grooms off the mites that trouble other bees. Real species: Apis cerana.
reason: My proposal for the third step, now that D82 has cut the giant honey bee: people really keep it in hives (in India, on a smaller scale than the honeybee). No hive bee is fiercer than the killer bee, so this step is about where you can keep bees rather than about stings; if you'd rather stop at two steps, it can go.

name: Black ants (the black garden ant)
change: Workers, scouts, warriors and the queen, near home. Real black garden ants have no soldier caste, so the warriors are workers that stay by the queen and the nest mouths and fight with bites and a spray of formic acid; old colonies really do raise bigger workers, which can make the guards look tougher. With aphids cut, they eat nectar and fruit, as real ones do. Real species: Lasius niger.
reason: Your settled ant (D39, D79), with warriors that are true to life.

name: Fire ants
change: Workers, warriors (the real big-headed soldiers) and the queen of the Deadly Ants zones. A mound with no entrance you can see boils over with stinging ants when it's touched, and the sting burns and blisters. Real fire ants survive floods as a living raft with the queen inside, a fact for their description. Real species: the red imported fire ant, Solenopsis invicta.
reason: Your far-ring ant (D39, D79). Fire ants really have soldiers, so their warriors are true to life.

name: Garden centipede (the stone centipede)
change: The village centipede, as now: the game's first real fight, lunging at anything warm. Its real kind, found under garden stones, is harmless to people and quick to run for cover, a fact for its description. Real species: Lithobius forficatus.
reason: The easy one of your three centipedes (D79).

name: Tiger centipede
change: The banded centipede of the Ant Colony and the Centipede Cavern's upper halls, hunting at night from burrows and from under rocks. After a bite its venom takes days to refill, so a tiger centipede that has just bitten hits weaker for a while. It lives by the Ant Colony and eats the ants. Real species: Scolopendra polymorpha.
reason: The middle centipede, and the answer to the "raid centipede": not a species, but centipedes living by the ants as part of the ecosystem.

name: Giant centipede (the Amazonian giant)
change: The deadly third, as the game already describes it: the Amazonian giant, the world's largest centipede, which hunts in caves by hanging from the ceiling and grabbing whatever passes. Its bite has killed a child. It lives in the Centipede Cavern's depths, the Millipede Forest and Spider Vale West: the forest and vale centipedes you kept from my cuts are this one, not two more kinds. Real species: Scolopendra gigantea.
reason: The dangerous third of your three (D79), and a hunt no other bug has: in the cavern you look up. If you'd rather choose by temper, the Vietnamese giant centipede is the alternative: aggressive and nervous, it strikes at any vibration, and its bite has also killed.

name: Garden millipede
change: As now: the slow rot-eater of the village. A real woodland kind (the American giant millipede) that coils up and oozes a fluid that burns the skin, so it is harmless if left alone. Real species: the American giant millipede, Narceus americanus.
reason: The easy one of your three millipedes (D79).

name: Giant African millipede
change: The big, armoured millipede of the Millipede Forest and the caves, the tougher cave millipede D21 wanted. It curls into a spiral and oozes a fluid that harms the eyes; in the game, a short spray when it's struck, so keep your distance or wear goggles. Real species: Archispirostreptus gigas.
reason: The middle millipede, with a different defence (armour and a fluid) rather than more health.

name: Shocking pink dragon millipede
change: The poisonous one, deep in the Millipede Forest: spiky and vivid pink, it gives off cyanide, and a struck one leaves a small poison cloud. Rain brings them out in numbers. Real species: Desmoxytes purpurosea.
reason: Your dangerous, poisonous millipede (D79). Real millipedes are slow and never hunt, so their danger is poison and numbers after rain; speed stays the centipedes' thing, which keeps the two families easy to tell apart. A fast millipede would be a liberty the game takes, if you still want one. For a night look instead, the glowing millipede is a cyanide millipede that glows blue-green all night.

name: Forest scorpion (the Asian forest scorpion)
change: The Wasp Thicket's scorpion: big, black and shiny, living under logs in the damp woods. It fights with its big claws, pinching and holding, and its sting hurts but rarely does more. Real species: Heterometrus spinifer.
reason: Your woodland scorpion (D79). It is a forest-living relative of the emperor scorpion, which was cut as a poor fit for the desert; in the woods it fits.

name: Fat-tailed scorpion
change: Scorpion Rocks' deadly scorpion: thin claws and a fat tail, hiding by day in cracks and under stones, at home in dry, rocky country rather than sand. Its venom is among the most dangerous of all scorpions. Real species: the yellow fat-tailed scorpion, Androctonus australis.
reason: Your dry-zone scorpion (D79). Big claws and a weak sting in the woods, thin claws and a deadly sting in the rocks: the pair shows a real rule of thumb at a glance. Scorpions really glow under ultraviolet light, so a blacklight lantern would be a fair night tool there.

name: Dragonfly (the blue dasher)
change: The beginner dragonfly, by the water on the village's west side: small and powder blue, it perches, darts out and points its tail at the sky. As in the game, it keeps the village wasps in check; real blue dashers eat hundreds of small insects a day, mosquitoes among them. Real species: Pachydiplax longipennis.
reason: Your beginner dragonfly (D79): easy to watch and catch.

name: Emperor dragonfly
change: The big blue dragonfly of the Butterfly Fields and the swamps: it rarely lands, and it hunts butterflies and other dragonflies in the air, a real threat to the player's butterflies. Real species: Anax imperator.
reason: Your medium dragonfly (D79); the game already has its picture.

name: Dragonhunter
change: The deadly dragonfly of the deep river: it hunts other dragonflies, swooping from above, and even eats monarchs, leaving their poisonous parts. Real species: Hagenius brevistylus.
reason: Your deadly dragonfly (D79), the hunter of hunters. Real dragonflies don't harm people, so its strike at a player is a liberty the game takes.

name: Meadow butterfly (the queen butterfly)
change: As now: the village's cartoonish milkweed butterfly, whose caterpillars grow up out in the world (D38). Its real name can be the queen butterfly, the monarch's milkweed cousin of meadows, fields and marshes: darker brown and plainer than a monarch, which suits the look you wanted. Real species: Danaus gilippus.
reason: Already the game's butterfly; the real name is my suggestion, since every bug needs one (D80).

name: Monarch
change: The orange milkweed butterfly of the Butterfly Fields: its caterpillars store the milkweed's poison, so few things eat it, and monarchs rest together in great clusters. Real species: Danaus plexippus.
reason: Fine to have (D79), and it plays differently from the village butterfly: poisonous, and gathering in crowds.

name: Purple emperor
change: The woodland butterfly of the Wasp Thicket's oaks: it lives high in the trees and comes down for rot, sap and droppings, not flowers, so bait brings it down, as old collectors did. The males flash purple only at some angles. Real species: Apatura iris.
reason: Your woodland butterfly (D79), with a catch that takes planning, and a food link to the carrion beetle.

name: Luna moth
change: The big pale-green moth with long tails, out at night in the Butterfly Fields and the Thicket. The adult never eats and lives about a week. Real species: Actias luna.
reason: The best-known moth, the night partner of the meadow butterfly.

name: Death's-head hawkmoth
change: A big moth with a skull-like mark on its back that raids beehives for honey at night in the Bee Meadow, squeaking, perhaps to pass as a queen bee. Its caterpillars eat plants of the tomato family, the player's tomatoes and eggplants among them. Real species: Acherontia atropos.
reason: The hawk moth (D79) as the famous one; it ties the moths to the player's bees and crops.

name: Emperor moth
change: A big eyespotted moth of heath and moor. Real species: Saturnia pavonia.
reason: One of your candidates (D79). The luna moth and the death's-head already cover the night moths, so I'd leave it out unless the Butterfly Fields' design wants it.

name: Silk moth (the silkworm)
change: The farm moth: tamed for 5,000 years, it can't fly or live wild, and its caterpillars eat only mulberry leaves. One cocoon is a single thread hundreds of metres long. Raised for silk; it needs a mulberry tree. Real species: Bombyx mori.
reason: The truest livestock bug there is, and the honest source of silk: the silk rows I wrote took silk from luna and emperor moths, whose silk people don't really harvest.

name: Carrion beetle (the burying beetle)
change: As now: the beetle that clears the dead. Real burying beetles bury small carcasses, and both parents raise their young on them; in the game the carcasses are dead bugs, which vanish into the ground. The mites they carry eat fly eggs, a link to the fly farm. Real species: a burying beetle, Nicrophorus vespilloides.
reason: Already the game's beetle; the real name brings a lovely, true behaviour.

name: Cave beetle
change: A blind, wingless, round-backed beetle of cold caves that eats what drifts in with the water. Its kind, found in 1831, was the first cave beetle ever described. Real species: Leptodirus hochenwartii.
reason: Your cave beetle (D79), with a real species and a great fact for the first cave.

name: Rhinoceros beetle (the Hercules beetle)
change: The Millipede Forest's mini-boss: it grabs a rival between its two horns, lifts it and throws it. Its horn makes the Beetle-Horn Maul. Real species: Dynastes hercules.
reason: Your horned beetle (D75, D79), with a ready-made boss attack from its real fighting.

name: Stag beetle
change: The antler-jawed beetle of the Wasp Thicket woods: males lock jaws and wrestle to push each other off logs. Real species: Lucanus cervus.
reason: A fair, readable fight in the middle ring, apart from the Hercules beetle's forest.

name: Colorado beetle
change: The Locust Farmland's crop pest: orange with black stripes, it strips tomatoes and eggplants and breeds several times a summer. Ground beetles and tiny wasps are its real enemies. Real species: Leptinotarsa decemlineata.
reason: The crop beetle (D79) as the real crop destroyer of the American West, for the western-style farm town.

name: Bombardier beetle
change: A small beetle of the Hilltop Meadow that fires a boiling spray from its tail, about 20 shots before it runs dry. Real species: Brachinus crepitans.
reason: A one-of-a-kind "don't fight it head-on" lesson, and one you can wear out.

name: Termites (mound-building termites)
change: Mound-building termites of the dry far ring (the Locust Farmland, Scorpion Rocks): they farm a fungus inside their mounds for food, and the fungus's warmth helps heat the nest. In Africa people really eat the winged ones, dried or ground into flour. Real species: Macrotermes.
reason: Cut: it wouldn't fit the game's mechanics (D80).

name: Stick insect (the Indian stick insect)
change: The twig-like insect of the Wasp Thicket woods: it sways like a leaf in the wind, so it's hard to spot, and a kept female lays eggs with no male at all. Real species: Carausius morosus.
reason: Cut (D80).

name: Cave spider (the European cave spider)
change: The spider of the lower underground, near cave mouths and in tunnels: it hates light, drops onto prey on a single thread, eats millipedes and centipedes, and hangs white teardrop egg sacs from cave roofs. Real species: Meta menardi.
reason: Your small cave spider (D21, D79), with real cave habits; smaller than the vales' spiders.

name: Daddy longlegs
change: The harmless long-legged bug of both Spider Vales, the caves and the woods: it gathers in clusters of thousands, and a dropped leg keeps twitching to distract hunters. It isn't a true spider, which its description can say. Real species: the eastern harvestman, Leiobunum vittatum.
reason: Under the plain name you chose (D79), and the slow, long-legged one you pictured for Spider Vale: a calm bug among the vales' hunters.

name: Wolf spider
change: Spider Vale West's everyday hunter: no web, it chases or waits at a burrow; its eyes shine back at a torch at night, and the mother carries her young on her back. Real species: the Carolina wolf spider, Hogna carolinensis.
reason: A hunting spider for the west vale (D79), with a real night tell: the eyeshine.

name: Jumping spider
change: The small, harmless jumper of Spider Vale West and the Butterfly Fields, with big front eyes; it leaps several body lengths on a safety thread. Real species: the bold jumping spider, Phidippus audax.
reason: A hunting spider players love, and a calm bug in a dangerous vale, so not everything there attacks.

name: Brazilian wandering spider
change: Spider Vale West's real danger: it wanders the ground at night instead of building webs, and rears up its front legs in a swaying threat. Real species: Phoneutria nigriventer.
reason: The west vale needs one truly dangerous spider, and this one is real and rarely, but truly, deadly.

name: Black widow
change: Spider Vale East: a tangled web low down, easy to avoid but dangerous if you blunder into it. Real species: the southern black widow, Latrodectus mactans.
reason: Your spider (D79).

name: Tarantula (the Goliath tarantula)
change: A huge tarantula of deep burrows in the east vale: it hisses by rubbing its legs and flicks irritating hairs at whatever bothers it. It is also called the Goliath birdeater, an old name. Real species: Theraphosa blondi.
reason: The tarantula (D79), with two real defences to learn.

name: Giant huntsman
change: A fast spider of the caves of Spider Vale East that runs sideways, like a crab, and ambushes from the walls. Real species: Heteropoda maxima.
reason: The giant huntsman (D79): real, found only in 2001 in caves, and set apart by its speed.

name: Marsh mosquito (the house mosquito)
change: The Shallow Swamp's mosquito: it bites at dusk and lays floating rafts of eggs on still water, so sand laid on the marsh really holds it back. Like every mosquito it drinks nectar; it bites people, and one form of it lays its first eggs with no blood meal at all. Real species: Culex pipiens.
reason: The easier of the two mosquitoes I suggest for the swamps (the mosquito is kept, D79).

name: Swamp mosquito (the malaria mosquito)
change: The Deep Swamp's dangerous mosquito: it rests with its tail tipped up, and its young lie flat on marsh water, so sand holds it back too. Real ones bite quietly at dusk and at night; the lunging and swarming are the game's own. Real ones also seek out caterpillars and drink their body fluid, which kept them alive longer in a 2014 study, though it did not show them laying eggs from it. Real species: the common malaria mosquito, Anopheles quadrimaculatus.
reason: Your later-stage mosquito (D79), and the answer to what the swamps' mosquitoes feed on: people, nectar, and, as a small stretch of that real behaviour, the body fluid of caterpillars and other soft bugs. Which soft bugs live in the swamps is for their design. The game already has its picture.

name: Water strider
change: The bug that walks on water, in the swamps and on the village lake; it feels for prey through ripples and eats mosquito larvae. Real species: the common pond skater, Gerris lacustris.
reason: Under its plain name (D79): a calm, beautiful water bug and a real check on the mosquitoes, alongside sand and the dragonflies.

name: Crayfish (the red swamp crayfish)
change: The farmed crayfish of the swamps and the village lake: it digs mud burrows and is raised in ponds, the real crawfish of a crawfish boil. The fish trap catches it. Real species: Procambarus clarkii.
reason: The crayfish (D79) that carries the game's fish trap and crayfish boil truthfully: a real livestock crustacean.

name: River crab
change: A freshwater crab of the Underground River and the deep river: aggressive, and nine in ten attack with the big right claw, so watch the right claw. Real species: Potamon fluviatile.
reason: The crab (D79), with a real, readable tell, in place of an invented armoured crab.

name: Praying mantis (the Chinese mantis)
change: The big mantis of the Locust Farmland and the Thicket's edges: an ambush hunter that takes hornets and grasshoppers. Its egg cases come from the game's own mantises (D80): a player who keeps mantises sets their egg cases out against the locusts, as gardeners really buy them to protect gardens. Real species: Tenodera sinensis.
reason: The mantis (D79, D80) as a farm tool from real life, and an enemy of the locust from the ecosystem.

name: Orchid mantis
change: A pink-and-white mantis shaped like a flower, in the Butterfly Fields: it draws in more pollinators than real flowers do, and eats butterflies. Real species: Hymenopus coronatus.
reason: The mantis family's second kind, playing completely differently: a hunter you mistake for a flower, and a quiet danger to the player's butterflies.

name: House cricket
change: The farm cricket: farmed today for food and animal feed, ground into cricket flour; small and easy to raise. Real species: Acheta domesticus.
reason: It carries the cricket protein drink truthfully and is an easy livestock bug; a maybe for now (D80).

name: Field cricket
change: The black meadow cricket of the Bee and Hilltop Meadows: the male sings at the door of his burrow and defends it fiercely. Real species: Gryllus campestris.
reason: The wild cricket (D79), with a small, readable behaviour.

name: Firefly
change: As now: fireflies flash a code of their own kind, and their larvae glow too. Real species: the common eastern firefly, Photinus pyralis.
reason: Already the game's firefly.

name: Cave glowworm (the New Zealand glowworm)
change: The cave light: a fly larva that hangs sticky fishing lines from cave ceilings and lures small flying insects with its glow, cave flies on the wing among them. A ceiling of them over the Underground River. Real species: Arachnocampa luminosa.
reason: Your glowworm (D21, D49, D79), as the real cave glowworm.

name: Locust (the desert locust)
change: Green and solitary most of the time; when they crowd together after rain brings a flush of green, they turn yellow and black and swarm, first as marching bands of young, then as flying swarms. Thinning them early, by harvesting them or with mantises, heads it off. Real species: the desert locust, Schistocerca gregaria.
reason: Your locust (D42, D62, D63, D79), with the swarm as a real change that has a cause, never a random event.
